title: sdfcube water-water (identical), chained 6 times
purpose: Exercises `sdfcube` [@epsrmanual], which computes the spatial density function of one molecule type around another directly on a 3D grid for visualisation, including accumulation of the cube over a chained run.
system: The EPSR-test configuration `200DMSO400Water.ato`: 200 DMSO (atoms S, C, C, O, 6 H) and 400 water molecules (O1, H1, H1; SPC/E parameters [@berendsen1987]), 3200 atoms at 300 K in a cubic box of side 33.12 Å, a model of the DMSO-water mixtures of Soper and Luzar [@soperluzar1992]. `sdfcube` histograms the centres of the second molecules, rotated into the frame of each central molecule (Euler angles from the axis definitions), on a cubic grid and writes the spatial density function as a Gaussian `.cube` file together with the averaged molecules (`-first.xyz`, `-second.xyz`). Here water around water (centre = mass centre of O1/H1, z axis to the H-H midpoint, y from H 2) on a 17×17×17 grid (`mpixel 8`, `rmax 6`: 0.75 Å steps, stored in bohr in the cube header).
inputs: Input files written by hand from the keyword tables (`setup_symbols_*`), one `keyword value` per line, ended by `q`; `200DMSO400Water.ato` copied from EPSR-test. `water.SDFCUBE.dat` with `nsumt 0`, `averagemol y`.
verification: Six passes. Pass 1 creates `water.SDFCUBE.cube`; pass 6 (`nsumt 5`) reads the step size and the old cube (`initcube`, `outcube`) and forms `fc1*old + fc*new`; final `nsumt 6`. The cube, both xyz files and the updated input file are compared after each pass. No `sharm`/`sdf` patch is involved.
notes: Reproduced Fortran behaviour: `fc1` is computed from an uninitialised variable that gfortran -O2 folds to 1.0 (checked in the reference object code); for identical molecules `averagemol` is read from the `axiss1` value (missing `iref=iref+2`), so a single molecule is written to the xyz files.
